A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SGD/Richardson-Romberg study. Their complete main texts, Figure 1, equations, and Appendices A-E are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Figure 1 report original simulations on f(theta)=theta^2+cos(theta), averaged over 320 runs. Appendix E supplies experimental details.

after.justification: Section 5, Figure 1, and Appendix E retain the original simulation results and their experimental setting.

M1.justification: Both versions use synchronously driven SGD chains with step sizes gamma and 2gamma, tail averaging, and the same Richardson-Romberg combination. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same one-dimensional objective theta^2+cos(theta) with additive standard Gaussian gradient noise. No datasets, tasks, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically benchmarks external algorithms. Figure 1 retains RR error and its diagnostic with the leading noise term removed; Root-SGD remains a theoretical literature comparison.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E retain n=250*2^k for k=0,...,14, gamma=n^(-1/2), the paired 2gamma trajectory, and the same squared-error and rescaled-error evaluations.

E4.justification: The same Figure 1 analysis removes the leading noise term and rescales errors to examine the predicted remainder rate. No ablations, robustness tests, or supplementary empirical analyses are added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging over 320 independent parallel runs. Neither adds seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figure 1 contains identical plotted results. Both versions report squared-remainder scaling of n^(-3/2), corresponding to n^(-3/4) in root-MSE; no empirical result entries change.

T1.justification: Theorems 3 and 15 replace sixth-moment assumptions A3(6)/C1(6) with fourth-moment assumptions and adjust the step-size conditions accordingly. The distance-like definition replaces the truncated distance power with d_Z(x,y)^q. Lemma 11 corrects F to its gradient, and Lemma 24 adds an absolute constant to its bound. These are localized revisions; the main RR theorems and convergence rates remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: an optimal leading covariance term, an n^(-3/4) second-order root-MSE term, higher-moment bounds, and weighted Wasserstein geometric ergodicity.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 newly explains the covariance relationship and conversion from Hessian-scaled error bounds to parameter-error bounds. Section 4 removes the tau-mixing assertion and discussion of why Merlevede et al. (2011) cannot be directly applied. The principal smoothness, convexity, and noise limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix E retains the same experimental instructions and code-repository link. No implementation, hardware, runtime, or resource-access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2 explicitly adds the already-cited Dieuleveut et al. (2020) among RR-SGD antecedents. The Merlevede et al. (2011) discussion and reference are removed. Durmus et al. changes from 2024 to 2025 publication metadata for the same work.

P1.justification: Localized prose and notation edits include expanded covariance and coupling explanations and renamed bias constants. The main section and appendix organization is retained. Acknowledgments become unnumbered and add Belomestny to the funding acknowledgment.

P2.justification: Equation layouts receive local adjustments, including placing psi and G side by side in Section 4 and expanding the duality display in Appendix D.1. Figure 1, including its axes, legends, and caption, is unchanged; no figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: The weaker assumptions in Theorems 3/15, corrected gradient expressions, and clearer covariance and proof explanations modestly improve precision and readability. A countervailing defect is incomplete constant renaming: Theorems 17/23 retain C1 after its definition becomes Cb,2. This local inconsistency limits the improvement; the main RR results and empirical support remain unchanged.
